sentences.en: VOA Learning English presents America's Presidents.
sentences.zh: 美国之音英语学习节目为您带来“美国总统”系列。

sentences.en: Today we are talking about George Washington.
sentences.zh: 今天我们聊聊乔治·华盛顿。

sentences.en: He was the first president of the United States.
sentences.zh: 他是美国第一任总统。

sentences.en: He served from 1789 to 1797.
sentences.zh: 他在位时间为1789年至1797年。

sentences.en: But he had many other accomplishments, too.
sentences.zh: 不过，他还有许多其他成就。

sentences.en: He owned thousands of hectares of land in his home state of Virginia.
sentences.zh: 他在家乡弗吉尼亚州拥有数千公顷土地。

sentences.en: He was a famous general, who led the American colonists to freedom from British rule.
sentences.zh: 他是一位著名的将军，曾领导美国殖民者摆脱英国的统治获得自由。

sentences.en: And he presided over the convention that created the U.S. Constitution.
sentences.zh: 他还主持了制定美国宪法的制宪会议。

sentences.en: For Washington, that was enough.
sentences.zh: 对华盛顿来说，这就足够了。

sentences.en: He said he wanted to retire from public service and return home.
sentences.zh: 他说他想退出公共服务，回到家乡。

sentences.en: But the country’s new electors had other ideas.
sentences.zh: 但国家的新任选举人却另有想法。

sentences.en: They wanted him to move to New York and invent the American presidency.
sentences.zh: 他们想让他搬到纽约，去开创美国的总统职位。

sentences.en: Washington accepted the job as his duty.
sentences.zh: 华盛顿把这份职务视为自己的职责而接受下来。

sentences.en: Washington was sworn in as president in 1789.
sentences.zh: 华盛顿于1789年宣誓就任总统。

sentences.en: At the time, a truly united states was still just an idea.
sentences.zh: 当时，一个真正统一的国家还只是一个理念。

sentences.en: Americans were unconnected groups.
sentences.zh: 美国人还是彼此互不相连的群体。

sentences.en: They came from different countries, had different religions, and spoke different languages.
sentences.zh: 他们来自不同国家，信仰不同宗教，说着不同语言。

sentences.en: For example, a quarter of the people in the state of Pennsylvania spoke only German.
sentences.zh: 例如，在宾夕法尼亚州，有四分之一的人只说德语。

sentences.en: Doug Bradburn is the founding director of the Washington Library at Mount Vernon.
sentences.zh: 道格·布拉德伯恩是费尔芒特华盛顿图书馆的创始馆长。

sentences.en: He says when Washington took office, the country was “fragile.”
sentences.zh: 他说，当华盛顿就职时，这个国家“脆弱不堪”。

sentences.en: “The chances that it would even survive were probably very, very slim.”
sentences.zh: “它甚至能够存活下来的可能性可能非常、非常渺茫。”

sentences.en: Bradburn explains that Washington had to establish social and political unity.
sentences.zh: 布拉德本解释说，华盛顿必须建立社会和政治上的团结。

sentences.en: But the Constitution did not say how the president could do that.
sentences.zh: 但是宪法并没有说明总统该如何做到这一点。

sentences.en: So, Bradburn says, George Washington invented the job for all future presidents.
sentences.zh: 因此，布拉德本说，乔治·华盛顿为未来的所有总统“发明”了这个职务。

sentences.en: He established a group of advisors — called the cabinet—as well as the nation’s official money.
sentences.zh: 他组建了一个顾问团——称为内阁——同时也确立了国家的官方货币。

sentences.en: He appointed a six-member Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 他任命了六名大法官组成最高法院。

sentences.en: And he created the Department of Foreign Affairs, now called the State Department.
sentences.zh: 他还设立了外交部，即现在的国务院。

sentences.en: However, Washington said it was the president’s responsibility to set foreign policy.
sentences.zh: 然而，华盛顿说，制定外交政策是总统的责任。

sentences.en: Historian Doug Bradburn explains that Washington established the president not just as a figurehead, but as a decision maker.
sentences.zh: 历史学家道格·布拉德本解释说，华盛顿确立的总统不仅仅是名义上的象征，而是真正的决策者。

sentences.en: But he always used the Constitution as his guide.
sentences.zh: 不过他始终以宪法作为自己的指导。

sentences.en: “He wasn’t just trying to establish an office and then figure out a way to justify it, he was trying to work with his Constitution.”
sentences.zh: “他不只是试图建立一个职位，然后想办法为它辩护，他是在努力依据自己的宪法来行事。”

sentences.en: George Washington was born in 1732 in the colony of Virginia.
sentences.zh: 乔治·华盛顿于1732年出生于弗吉尼亚殖民地。

sentences.en: His father died when George was 11 years old.
sentences.zh: 当乔治11岁时，他的父亲去世了。

sentences.en: As a boy, he learned reading, writing and math.
sentences.zh: 少年时，他学习了阅读、写作和数学。

sentences.en: Then he worked as a land surveyor in western Virginia.
sentences.zh: 之后，他在弗吉尼亚西部从事土地测量师的工作。

sentences.en: Historian Joseph Ellis points out that Washington did not have a formal education.
sentences.zh: 历史学家约瑟夫·埃利斯指出，华盛顿没有受过正规教育。

sentences.en: Instead of going to college, Ellis says, Washington went to war.
sentences.zh: 埃利斯说，华盛顿没有上大学，而是走上了战场。

sentences.en: He fought against the French and Indians as a British Army officer.
sentences.zh: 他作为英国陆军军官，与法国人和印第安人作战。

sentences.en: That experience informed Washington’s world view.
sentences.zh: 这段经历影响了华盛顿的世界观。

sentences.en: Ellis describes the first president as “a realist.”
sentences.zh: 埃利斯把第一任总统描述为“一个现实主义者”。

sentences.en: At the same time, Washington was a “very passionate man” with “extremely strong emotions.”
sentences.zh: 与此同时，华盛顿是一个"感情非常充沛"的人，"情感极为强烈"。

sentences.en: He was known to get angry, but he showed his temper to only a few people.
sentences.zh: 他容易发怒，但他只对少数表露过脾气。

sentences.en: Washington not only acted like a great leader – he looked like one.
sentences.zh: 华盛顿不仅举止伟岸，外表也颇具领袖风范。

sentences.en: George Washington stood about 1.9 meters tall.
sentences.zh: 乔治·华盛顿身高约1.9米。

sentences.en: That was a head taller than the average man of his time.
sentences.zh: 这比当时普通男子高出一个头。

sentences.en: He was very strong, and very graceful.
sentences.zh: 他体魄强健，举止优雅。

sentences.en: He was known as one of the best horseback riders and best dancers in Virginia.
sentences.zh: 他以弗吉尼亚最优秀的骑手和舞者著称。

sentences.en: But he had a problem: bad teeth.
sentences.zh: 但他有个麻烦：牙齿不好。

sentences.en: Unlike his wife, Martha, who was known for her lovely smile, George Washington began losing his teeth in his twenties.
sentences.zh: 与以迷人微笑著称的妻子玛莎不同，乔治·华盛顿二十多岁就开始掉牙。

sentences.en: When he was sworn in as president, he had only one tooth left.
sentences.zh: 就任总统宣誓时，他只剩一颗牙。

sentences.en: Washington remains an important figure in the American imagination.
sentences.zh: 华盛顿至今仍是美国人想象中一个重要人物。

sentences.en: Even today people tell stories about him.
sentences.zh: 直到今天，人们仍在讲述关于他的故事。

sentences.en: One popular story, that he had wooden teeth, is not true.
sentences.zh: 其中一个流行的说法——说他戴着假牙——并不属实。

sentences.en: But he did wear dentures.
sentences.zh: 但他确实戴过假牙。

sentences.en: They were made, in part, from hippopotamus ivory.
sentences.zh: 这些假牙部分由河马象牙制成。

sentences.en: And he did not chop down a cherry tree as a child and then admit it by saying, “I cannot tell a lie.”
sentences.zh: 他小时候并没有砍倒樱桃树，然后说"我不能说谎"来承认错误。

sentences.en: In fact, historian Joseph Ellis says George Washington “lied many times.”
sentences.zh: 事实上，历史学家约瑟夫·埃利斯称乔治·华盛顿"撒过多次谎"。

sentences.en: But it is true that as Washington became more famous, his reputation grew.
sentences.zh: 但确实的是，随着华盛顿越来越有名，他的声誉也随之增长。

sentences.en: People thought of him as a man who always did the right thing.
sentences.zh: 人们把他看作一个总是做正确之事的人。

sentences.en: Joseph Ellis says even Washington understood people would look at his writings and judge him.
sentences.zh: 约瑟夫·埃利斯说，就连华盛顿也明白人们会阅读他的著作并据此评判他。

sentences.en: “Washington went from being a man to a monument.
sentences.zh: "华盛顿从一个有血有肉的人变成了一座纪念碑。

sentences.en: He was aware of the fact that he had a role to play and that all emerging nations need mythical heroes.”
sentences.zh: 他意识到自己肩负着某种使命，也意识到所有新兴的国家都需要神话般的英雄。"

sentences.en: Washington became very protective of his personal thoughts.
sentences.zh: 华盛顿对自己的私人想法变得极为保护。

sentences.en: His wife burned most of their letters.
sentences.zh: 他的妻子烧掉了他们大部分的信件。

sentences.en: Yet we know a little bit about George Washington’s thoughts from other writing.
sentences.zh: 然而，我们从其他文字中了解了关于乔治·华盛顿想法的一些点滴。

sentences.en: One of his regrets, he said, was that he had not done something to end slavery.
sentences.zh: 他说，他的一大遗憾是他没有采取任何行动来废除奴隶制。

sentences.en: Like many plantation owners, Washington was a slave holder.
sentences.zh: 像许多种植园主一样，华盛顿也是蓄奴者。

sentences.en: More than 300 enslaved people lived on his property.
sentences.zh: 有超过300名被奴役的人生活在他的产业上。

sentences.en: By the end of his life, Washington opposed slavery.
sentences.zh: 到他生命的尽头，华盛顿反对奴隶制。

sentences.en: He left a will ordering his survivors to free his slaves after his wife’s death.
sentences.zh: 他在遗嘱中命令他的继任者在妻子去世后释放他的奴隶。

sentences.en: Washington’s will became relevant sooner than he might have liked.
sentences.zh: 华盛顿的遗嘱比他希望的更早地变得相关。

sentences.en: Three years after he finished his second term as president, Washington fell ill.
sentences.zh: 在他完成第二任总统任期后的三年，华盛顿生病了。

sentences.en: He had been outside riding his horse on a cold, wet day.
sentences.zh: 那天又冷又湿，他一直在外面骑马。

sentences.en: When he came home, he complained of a sore throat.
sentences.zh: 当他回到家时，他抱怨喉咙痛。

sentences.en: Over the next two days, his condition became worse.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的两天里，他的病情恶化了。

sentences.en: On December 14, 1799, he died in his bed, surrounded by his wife, enslaved maids, and friends.
sentences.zh: 1799年12月14日，他在床上去世，周围环绕着他的妻子、被奴役的女仆和朋友们。

sentences.en: He was 67.
sentences.zh: 他享年67岁。

sentences.en: Historian Joseph Ellis says one of the best things about George Washington was his ability to give up power.
sentences.zh: 历史学家约瑟夫·埃利斯说，乔治·华盛顿最好的品质之一是他放弃权力的能力。

sentences.en: At the end of the Revolutionary War, General Washington returned his sword.
sentences.zh: 在独立战争结束时，华盛顿将军交还了他的剑。

sentences.en: And at the end of his administration, President Washington simply returned home.
sentences.zh: 而在他的任期结束时，华盛顿总统只是回到了家。

sentences.en: “You could trust Washington with power because he was so conspicuously willing to give it up.”
sentences.zh: “你可以把权力交给华盛顿，因为他格外情愿放弃权力。”

sentences.en: Doug Bradburn says Washington was the right man at the right time.
sentences.zh: 道格·布拉德布恩认为，华盛顿是适逢其时的合适人选。

sentences.en: Bradburn, like many historians, calls George Washington the “indispensable man.”
sentences.zh: 布拉德布恩和许多历史学家一样，把乔治·华盛顿称为“不可或缺的人物”。

sentences.en: In other words, Washington was essential to the American experiment in self-government.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，华盛顿对美国自治实验至关重要。

sentences.en: He made ideas about American freedom real, and he showed that even the president would operate under the rule of law.
sentences.zh: 他让关于美国自由的理念成为现实，并表明连总统也要在法治之下运作。

sentences.en: I'm Kelly Jean Kelly.
sentences.zh: 我是凯利·简·凯利。

glossary.def: a person who is called the head of something but who has no real power
a person whose job is to measure and examine an area of land
the tendency of someone to become angry
moving in a smooth and attractive way
a legal document in which a person states who should receive his or her possessions after he or she dies
very easy to see or notice

glossary.zh: 不可或缺的；必不可少的
